text: Anxiety • If excessive worry causes impaired function/distress for at least 6 months with ≥ 3 of: muscle tension, restlessness, irritability, difficulty sleeping, poor concentration, tiredness, generalised anxiety disorder likely 160. • If anxiety is induced by a particular situation/object (phobia)

(No SNOMED concept for generic impaired function was found by search; the rule should at least note this or use the and-with-Distress as a documented approximation.)

Bullet 2 (phobia / panic): nothing is encoded. The page names two conditions ('induced by a particular situation/object (phobia)', 'repeated sudden fear with physical symptoms and no obvious cause (panic)') and the house standard treats a named condition the page wants recognised as at least a possible diagnosis or a check_for item. SNOMED has (snomed_concept "Phobia" "finding"), (snomed_concept "Panic attack" "finding") and (snomed_concept "Panic disorder" "disorder"). The 'discuss/refer' action itself is a management step and out of scope.
detail.problem: Part-by-part: (1) GAD likely: PARTIAL. Duration '(>= (onset Worried+Excessive) (time_ago 6 months))' correctly means onset at least 6 months ago; 'excessive worry' as Worried with qualifier Excessive is a fair encoding; the '>= 3 of 6' is enumerated exactly (A+any2(rest) | B+any2(rest) | C+any2(rest) | D+E+F covers every 3-subset of {muscle tension, restlessness, irritability, difficulty sleeping, poor concentration, tiredness}); the six symptom concepts map correctly (tiredness -> Fatigue, irritability -> Feeling irritable). Only the impaired-function alternative is missing. (2) Phobia/panic: MISSING (see parts_missing). (3) PTSD likely: CORRECT. '> 1 month' is encoded as (>= (onset Anxiety) (time_ago 1 months)), which is 'at least 1 month' rather than strictly more; immaterial. 'linked to a bad experience' -> Victim of psychological trauma is a reasonable concept (parent: Victim of trauma). The four groups (nightmares/flashbacks; avoids situations/people; on guard/easily startled; numb/detached from others/surroundings) are each an (or ...) so a group counts once, and '>= 3 of 4' is enumerated exactly as (G1 and any2(G2,G3,G4)) or (G2 and G3 and G4). 'feels numb/detached from others/surroundings' -> Emotionally detached + Derealization is a fair split. All concepts exist as named. The '-> 160' and 'discuss/refer' are out of scope.

text: The page's condition is 'excessive worry causes impaired function/distress'; the rule ANDs Distress unconditionally, dropping the impaired-function alternative. The rule is therefore stricter than the page: a patient with 6+ months of excessive worry, functional impairment and >= 3 symptoms but no recorded Distress gets no GAD diagnosis. If no SNOMED concept for functional impairment can be found, the approximation should be documented; otherwise add it as an (or Distress <impairment>) alternative.

The page's second Anxiety bullet names phobia and panic as recognisable patterns ('induced by a particular situation/object (phobia)'; 'repeated sudden fear with physical symptoms and no obvious cause (panic)') and nothing in the file captures either: no check_for item, no possible diagnosis. (snomed_concept "Phobia" "finding") and (snomed_concept "Panic attack" "finding") exist. A possible rule or at least check_for items would match the house standard's 'consider X' treatment; the discuss/refer action itself is out of scope.
